LESSON: READING 9.2.1 INTENSIVE READING

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: ENGLISH LANGUAGE
Strand: Strand 9
Topic 9.2: Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 3

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading, part of Strand 9 in Grade 4 ENGLISH LANGUAGE.

Key inquiry question: Why do we read narratives? 2. What makes you enjoy reading a narrative?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. read a short narrative of about 320 words for comprehension,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. apply appropriate reading strategies to read a narrative of about 320 words for information,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. appreciate reading for purposes of comprehension and information.

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. read a short narrative of about 320 words for comprehension,

   Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

B. apply appropriate reading strategies to read a narrative of about 320 words for information,

   Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

C. appreciate reading for purposes of comprehension and information.

   Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading helps learners achieve this outcome through discussion, practice, and activities at school. Think about how this applies in daily life in Kenya — at home, on the farm, in town, or at school.

D. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. read a passage in print or non-print format and answer questions,

2. discuss vocabulary from the passage and use them to construct simple sentences,

3. answer factual and inferential questions from a passage collaboratively,

4. give the sequence of events in a given story or passage,

5. read a digital text online or offline and collaborate in answering questions with peers. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. read a passage in print or non-print format and answer questions,
2. discuss vocabulary from the passage and use them to construct simple sentences,
3. answer factual and inferential questions from a passage collaboratively,
4. give the sequence of events in a given story or passage,
5. read a digital text online or offline and collaborate in answering questions with peers. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Reading 9.2.1 Intensive Reading together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
• Communication and Collaboration: This is enhanced as the learner answers factual and inferential questions in groups.

• Self-efficacy: This is achieved when the learner answers inferential and factual questions correctly.

Values:
Love: It is nurtured when the learner respects others as they read texts online or offline and answer questions.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Clubs and Societies: Reading clubs, writing clubs, journalism clubs among others build the learner’s self-esteem to become

more confident readers as they manoeuvre to give the sequence of events in a story.

Link to other Learning Areas:

The learner can link the content obtained from the theme of HIV and AIDS to concepts taught in Agriculture and,Science

and Technology.

Main points to remember:

1. read a short narrative of about 320 words for comprehension,
2. apply appropriate reading strategies to read a narrative of about 320 words for information,
3. appreciate reading for purposes of comprehension and information.

Remember the key question: Why do we read narratives? 2. What makes you enjoy reading a narrative?
